derivation.note: The month-over-month core print is the highest-variance single number for mortgage rates on the monthly calendar.

move.detail: +4 bp. Bigger in magnitude than 26% of the 54 moves since 2022-03-01. The typical move is 10.1 bp; this is 0.4 sigma.

insights.stat_line: Sitting in the top of its 1-year range, at the 82th percentile.

impact.meaning: A RISE in this series pushes mortgage rates UP. A fall pushes them DOWN.

chains.chain: Core CPI → ↑ Inflation expectations → ↑ 10Y Treasury → ↑ MBS yield → ↑ 30Y mortgage rate
rationales: Realised core inflation is the largest single input to forward inflation pricing.
The 10Y is a real yield plus an inflation expectation. Expectations move the nominal.
MBS are priced off the Treasury curve. This is the main channel.
Lenders price off MBS execution, with a short lag for rate sheets.

chains.chain: Core CPI → ↑ Fed policy stance → ↑ 2Y Treasury → ↑ 10Y Treasury → ↑ MBS yield → ↑ 30Y mortgage rate
rationales: Inflation is the Fed reaction function.
The front end prices the expected path of policy.
Front-end repricing pulls the belly and the long end, but only partly.
MBS are priced off the Treasury curve. This is the main channel.
Lenders price off MBS execution, with a short lag for rate sheets.

chains.chain: Core CPI → ↑ Fed policy stance → ↑ QT / MBS runoff → ↑ MBS spread → ↑ 30Y mortgage rate
rationales: Inflation is the Fed reaction function.
A hawkish Fed keeps runoff going.
Fed MBS runoff removes the largest price-insensitive buyer from the market.
A wider spread raises the borrower rate even when Treasuries are unchanged.
